content.value_statement: Pose and motion control workflows can be hard to route across image and video models. This skill selects the right RunComfy path and prepares clear CLI guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes video pose transfer requests to Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard.
Routes still image pose requests to Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA.
Supports Wan 2.2 Animate guidance for stylized character animation.
Builds RunComfy CLI input plans using hosted video, image, or control URLs.
Explains when multi-condition pose, depth, and canny workflows need RunComfy ComfyUI.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Uses hosted asset URLs; it does not create OpenPose or DWPose control images.
Complex multi-condition ControlNet stacks require RunComfy ComfyUI workflows, not the CLI endpoints.
Output quality depends on reference framing, motion clarity, and model limits.

use_cases.title: Transfer Choreography
use_cases.description: Apply a performer video to a target character image for draft or final motion-control video.

use_cases.title: Pose Lock an Illustration
use_cases.description: Use an OpenPose, DWPose, canny, or depth control image to guide a still generation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Model Route
use_cases.description: Compare RunComfy routes and choose the endpoint that matches asset type, style, and quality needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pose Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a still image from this hosted pose control image and prompt: [control URL], [prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Video Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer the motion from this reference video to this character image: [video URL], [image URL].

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the RunComfy route for this project: [video or still], [style], [control type], [quality target].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Control Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a pose workflow with pose, depth, and character reference. Tell me if CLI endpoints are enough.

output_examples.input: I have a dance reference video and a mascot image.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Kling Motion Control, asks for hosted asset URLs, and prepares motion-transfer CLI guidance.

output_examples.input: I want a portrait that follows my OpenPose skeleton.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA and describes the needed prompt and control image input.

output_examples.input: I need pose, depth, canny, and a character reference together.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that this needs a RunComfy ComfyUI workflow instead of the simple CLI routes.

best_practices: Use clean, single-subject reference videos with steady framing for motion transfer.
Host only assets you are allowed to send to RunComfy cloud endpoints.
Confirm model inputs before running the CLI, especially URLs, prompt text, and output directory.
anti_patterns: Do not send private or licensed assets without permission.
Do not use video motion routes for still image pose control.
Do not expect the CLI routes to handle pose, depth, canny, and reference images together.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It routes work through RunComfy cloud model endpoints using the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: What inputs do I need for video pose transfer?
faq.answer: You need a hosted reference video and a hosted target character image.

faq.question: What inputs do I need for still image pose control?
faq.answer: You need a prompt and a hosted control image, such as OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny.

faq.question: Can it create OpenPose or DWPose control images?
faq.answer: No. You must create the control image with another tool before using this skill.

faq.question: When should I use ComfyUI workflows instead?
faq.answer: Use ComfyUI workflows when you need multiple controls or richer graph-level customization.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy token?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI must be authenticated before model requests can run.
